_comment: Accepted findings for check-editor-render-parity.js (CHECK A: editor-canvas desync — a destructured+written attribute never referenced in the preview JSX; CHECK B: invalid CSS keyword passthrough — a SelectControl option value not in the target CSS property's valid keyword set). Same discipline as dead-controls-baseline.json: the guard reports NET-NEW findings only (findings NOT listed here). To accept a finding, add it here with a reason; to fix one, wire the attribute into the preview / correct the SelectControl option, then delete the entry. Empty `accepted` = zero tolerance once/if this is promoted to gate — it ships advisory-only today (2026-08-13), so nothing needs baselining yet; findings are census output, not a blocking backlog. CRITICAL: never raise the baseline silently — any increase must include a written reason (see check-element-manifest-conformance.js:796-798).

_meta.dispositionVocabularyNote: Closed vocabulary: by-design (correct, will never need fixing) / accepted-debt (real gap, consciously deferred) / detector-limitation (the checker itself is wrong — flags a rule violation per THE-MIGRATION-METHOD.md:455, not a normal outcome) / blocked (waiting on something external). See .claude/archive/parking.md P-BASELINE-DISPOSITION-VOCABULARY / .claude/LEDGER.md.

accepted.reason: Wave A1 ShadowControl redesign (2026-09-07): the resting boxShadow/boxShadowColour pair already has a canvas preview (resolveShadowPreviewComposed(), edit.js ~L339), but no SGS block canvas-previews a HOVER colour anywhere in the framework today — the editor canvas cannot simulate :hover without JS, and no shared mechanism for that exists yet. This attr existed under a different name (boxShadowHoverColour, a separate two-mount ShadowControl) before this session's rename+consolidation into one tabbed Normal/Hover mount; the underlying desync is pre-existing framework-wide debt (see sgs/product-search's 12 identical hover-colour-family findings, untouched by this session), surfaced under a new name by the rename rather than newly introduced.

Tier H Lottie background (Spec 38 §1.2a, D1151), same shape as the pre-existing bgVideo pair: bgLottie itself now has a real editor-canvas preview (background-preview.js's backgroundPreview() paints the same teal placeholder bgVideo gets, since the editor never mounts the real lottie-web player). bgLottieLoop controls only whether a MOUNTED player repeats after finishing — it has zero effect on the single static placeholder frame the editor renders, so there is nothing for a canvas preview to show. bgVideo has no equivalent loop attribute at all to compare against; this is the first background-media attribute where the loop flag is genuinely unpreviewable rather than just unbuilt.

Rotation timing (ms between messages) has no effect until Interactivity hydrates client-side; the editor canvas always shows a single static message, never a running rotation, so there is nothing for this value to visibly change.
The fade/slide transition only plays during a live client-side rotation swap; the static editor canvas never animates between messages, so there is no transition to preview.

Verified: this attribute IS read outside its own control (edit.js ~L297), but only to gate ANOTHER InspectorControls row (the rotation-arrow colour picker) -- still inside the checker's own 'control panel' boundary, never the canvas. The arrows themselves only render once Interactivity hydrates a running rotation, which the static canvas never does.
Pause-on-hover is client-side rotation behaviour (Interactivity) with no static-frame visual difference; the editor canvas cannot simulate a running, hoverable rotation.

Per the control's own help text ('Editor only -- never rendered on the frontend... shown in the editor list view only, so you can tell messages apart'): this is deliberately list-view-only metadata, not a canvas-visible property. It has no rendered counterpart to preview by design.

A link destination (the wishlist page URL, or a custom override) has no visual effect on the icon-link's own appearance -- the canvas icon+label+badge render identically regardless of where the link points, matching how other blocks' link-destination attrs are never canvas-previewed either.

Per the block's own file header: the editor shows a static 3-row PLACEHOLDER (sample data) -- the real wishlist state (empty or not) is only known client-side via the Store API, so the empty-state copy has nothing real to preview against in the editor's own request.
Same gap as emptyText (see that entry) -- the empty-state CTA only ever shows for a real empty wishlist, which the editor's static placeholder never represents.
